title: Synchronizing groups and weakly perfect graphs: a survey
summary: The concept of synchronization has been transferred from finite automata, via transformation semigroups, to permutation groups: a permutation group $G$ on a finite set $Ω$ is said to be synchronizing if, for any non-permutation $t$ on $Ω$, the transformation monoid $\langle G,t\rangle$ contains an element of rank~$1$. Synchronizing permutation groups are primitive and basic, and so are affine, diagonal, or almost simple (in the O'Nan--Scott classification).
